key_insight: Rather than generating 3D objects in one shot, 3D-ReGen conditions a generative model on an initial 3D shape (via a VecSet-based conditioning) to regenerate and refine geometry—enabling controlled enhancement, reconstruction, and editing from 2D images and an initial 3D seed.
problem_solved: Existing 3D generators offer limited controllability and cannot easily refine or edit a given 3D asset from additional 2D evidence; this work enables conditional, iterative regeneration of 3D geometry given an initial shape and images.
method: Introduce a conditioning mechanism (VecSet-based) that encodes an initial 3D shape as input context to a 3D regenerator.
Fuse 2D image cues and the conditioned initial shape to produce a regenerated 3D output, supporting enhancement, reconstruction, and editing workflows.
Unify multiple tasks (enhancement, reconstruction, editing) in a single regenerator model that refines geometry rather than synthesizing from scratch.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a controllable, unified tool to refine and edit 3D assets using 2D evidence and initial shapes—streamlining pipelines in graphics, AR/VR, robotics, and dataset augmentation while enabling iterative, user-driven 3D editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (initial 3D shape + 2D images) → VecSet conditioning → 3D-ReGen → regenerated 3D output
Before/after comparison grid showing initial vs. regenerated geometry (improvement/enhancement examples)
Task icons with brief examples: reconstruction (single/multi-view) , enhancement (denoising/detail fill), editing (shape manipulations)
Schematic of VecSet conditioning (abstract set-encoding visualization) to illustrate how the initial shape informs generation
paper_authors: Geon Yeong Park, Roman Shapovalov, Rakesh Ranjan, Jong Chul Ye, Andrea Vedaldi
